text.p: September T-bonds are on shakey ground and could slip to support at 113-22, technical analysts said on Thursday.

"If you look on an hourly basis, T-bond bollinger bands are quite flat," said Philippe Cahen, technical analyst at Credit Lyonnais in Paris. "Resistance comes in at 114-00 with support at the lower bollinger band at 113-22."
Bollinger bands are lines drawn at standard deviations around the price action to give support and resistance.
"I think we're most likely to go to the first support at 113-22," Cahen said.
By 0911 GMT, September T-bonds were down 3/32 at 113-26, just off the low of the session so far at 113-25.
Cahen noted that stochastics were overbought on an hourly basis but not on a daily one, suggesting the market could come back to the 114-00 level.
"But you have to be very careful. If the market is not going higher we could have a bearish divergence on a daily basis," he said. "If so, the main trend will be to the downside."
In that case, Cahen put support at 112-09, followed by a bigger prop at 110-18. "But we won't get there today," he added.
Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank in London, was more optimistic about the contract's prospects.
"For choice, the bias is still on the upside with choppy gains through 114-00 looking to set up 114-26 in the near term," he said in a note for clients.
He put minor support at 113-15/12, followed by a firmer platform at 113-02. Charts show the market hit a daily low of 113-12 on July 8.
By 0912 GMT, December Eurodollars were unchanged at 94.070.
